title: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an open-source tool to block exploits on running Linux systems before a patch
date_note: OpenAI's announcement is dated 23 November; Cyber Security News (24 November) gives 23 November as the launch day.
geo_basis: country named by the source; no city stated
summary: OpenAI says it and Cisco have open-sourced Shirudo, a runtime that uses eBPF 'shields' to block the code paths an exploit relies on in running Linux systems, without a restart, while a permanent fix is prepared. OpenAI describes one controlled test in which a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service. Cyber Security News notes the GitHub project is listed as pre-release.
plain: OpenAI and Cisco released an open-source tool that can block a specific exploit on a running Linux server without a restart, while a permanent patch is prepared. The GitHub project is listed as pre-release.
exec: OpenAI says Shirudo is meant to close the gap between learning of a vulnerability and fixing every affected system; the project is listed as pre-release.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Cyber Security News notes the shield does not replace the OpenJDK update.
impact: Tool release; one controlled test described.

validation.note: OpenAI's own announcement (primary) and Cyber Security News, which relays it and adds the pre-release status from GitHub.
